title: PiSPICE: Accelerating Post-Layout SPICE Simulation via Essential Parasitic Identification
problem: Post-layout SPICE simulation of advanced-node ICs involves billions to trillions of parasitic nodes, creating prohibitively high computational cost that slows design closure and verification cycles.
motivation: As feature sizes shrink and integration increases, post-layout simulations dominate design cycles, but directly analyzing billions of parasitic elements becomes computationally intractable, demanding smarter reduction approaches.
method: PiSPICE uses adjoint sensitivity analysis on pre-layout circuits to identify critical parasitic elements and eliminate non-critical ones. Only critical parasitics are retained in post-layout simulation; model order reduction minimizes their impact while non-critical parasitics are pruned entirely, dramatically reducing simulation scale.
key_novelty: First post-layout SPICE acceleration method using adjoint sensitivity analysis to identify essential parasitics on pre-layout circuits, avoiding expensive sensitivity computation on billion-node post-layout circuits and achieving 17.27x speedup.
contributions: Adjoint sensitivity analysis method for identifying critical parasitics on pre-layout circuits.
Model order reduction for non-critical parasitic impact minimization.
17.27x simulation speedup with <0.78% error vs commercial simulator Spectre.
primary_theme: post-layout SPICE acceleration via parasitic identification
